title: Scrubbing or pausing Live during a track start keeps music playing
acceptance: A seek, skip, or pause then resume during an in-flight Apple start ends playing or buffering at the new position (lane repro CM-01 passes for Apple). The Spotify half of CM-01 is RF-158.
Each singleton adapter exposes a settle signal (for example whenIdle()); runtime.enterTrack awaits it, bounded to about 3 s, and re-checks the epoch before prepare.
A never-settling previous call ends in a bounded, clearly worded error; existing runtime supersession tests still pass, and one new runtime test uses a real adapter with a lease.
Owner device check: audible scrub, pause and resume on iPhone Safari (Apple). The desktop Chrome check moved to RF-158 with the Spotify half.
Owner device check on iPhone Safari includes RF-123's owed check: when setQueue hangs, Retry playback recovers without a reload and without "still finishing a previous queue request".

Owner device check on iPhone Safari: tapping three timeline tracks within about 4 s ends playing the last tapped track, with neither "still finishing a cancelled play request" nor "still finishing a previous queue request".

The held Apple Music playback error (apple-music-adapter.ts onPlaybackError) carries an attempt token captured when the error fires and is delivered only if prepare, stop or destroy have not started a new attempt, with a test that a held error is dropped after destroy then prepare (RF-121 criterion 0).
nextAction: #669 merged as 0a77110 and is live on production (Worker 61cdeb33, SPA index-DTaSHnmL.js, HISTORY 2026-10-31). Stays For review until the owner's iPhone Safari device check: the 7 steps in the #669 PR body with ?playback-timing=1 (one Start, three timeline taps within about 4 s, quick taps, Next right after a start, one auto-advance), including whether WebKit keeps the gesture across the up-to-2 s wait. Criteria 0-2 and 6 are covered in code and mock tests; criteria 3-5 are the owed device checks. Spotify half: RF-158. Late-settle detection and clear-once: RF-159. Review follow-ups: RF-161.

evidence.summary: Proposed as packet 2 of the 2026-10-28 Claude audit at 4c344e2. Audit-only proposal; not reverified at intake.

AUD-001 (P2, confirmed with real adapters and runtime, fake SDKs): a Live seek, skip or pause then resume during a provider start puts the class in error and stops the clock. Repro and evidence files are listed in the audit package.
Owner set Ready in session on 2026-10-28.

Owner decision in session on 2026-10-28: Spotify work is reopened (the family now has Spotify Family). The Apple Music subscription ends around 2026-11-27, so Apple hardening and Apple device checks come first in that window.

Owner iPhone Safari Live on production d888d28 (Worker 765c9424, SPA index-BAVpF1uf.js), two screen recordings shared in session 2026-10-30, network not recorded. Start, Pause, Next and Previous worked. Tapping the class timeline to tracks 3, 4 and 5 within about 4 s showed "Playback stopped": first "Apple Music is still finishing a cancelled play request. Retry after it finishes, or reload.", then "The Apple Music player is still finishing a previous queue request for "Nookie"." Retry playback played Nookie about 2 s later, with no reload. Recordings are not stored in the repo.
Final review of #664 (RF-123), logged items 2 and 6: destroy() does not release the queue lock, and pendingPlays has the same never-settles shape as the queue lock before RF-123.
Owner set Ready in session on 2026-10-30 ("Yes, option 1, Apple hardening"): RF-108, RF-128 and RF-147 as one Apple hardening lane.

Apple hardening PR: SDK leases in apple-music-adapter.ts (a live owner's overlapping request still fails at once; a cancelled owner's setQueue/play is waited for, bounded 3 s from the cancel, then superseded (queue) or released with "did not finish a cancelled play request within 3 s. Retry playback." (play)); whenIdle() on the adapter contract; runtime.enterTrack waits for retired adapters, bounded 3 s, and re-checks the epoch before prepare; held-error attempt token.

New tests, all failing on main 5dd324a and passing on the PR: runtime with real adapters and leases ("taps to tracks 2 and 3 during a pending start end playing track 3 with no lock error"; "a start whose cancelled play never settles fails clearly, and Retry recovers without a reload"), lease tests for wait/supersede/release, and "drops a held playback error after destroy then prepare". "rejects an overlapping queue request while an older one is still pending" and the runtime supersession tests in runtime.test.ts pass unchanged. Mock MusicKit only; not audible playback.

Final review of #668 on 01dc417 found five significant bugs plus five cleanups; fixed in commit 05ad7ea on the same PR. A hung call no longer keeps whenIdle() pending (idle at timeout or at the settle bound; runtime retire entries expire too); the runtime waits only for retired adapters of the next track's provider; the late-settle snapshot is taken before setQueue is sent; a late settle after the track started re-cues and replays the playing song, or reports a Retry error if that fails; play() waits for a cancelled play after a re-cue. Eight new tests fail on 01dc417 and pass on 05ad7ea. Mock MusicKit only.

Owner decision in session 2026-10-30, relayed by the coordinator after the second final review of #668 on 6595d3f: option 1, remove automatic mid-track recovery. A late, superseded MusicKit settle after a track started shows the recoverable playback error (Retry) only while the track runs and never re-cues or plays on its own; while paused it is recorded and the next play re-cues; an unknown nowPlayingItem counts as fine.

Commit fe6a1d1 implements that decision and the other second-review fixes: lease check and claim in one synchronous step; fail() and destroy() retire adapters into a page-wide settle registry so Retry waits; a cancelled play past the bound stays tracked and Retry stops it, then waits one more bound; late settles decided by flags captured at settle time. Seven new tests fail on 6595d3f and pass on fe6a1d1; the in-time-rejection test passes on both (old microtask order happened to be right). Mock MusicKit only.

Owner decision in session 2026-10-30, relayed by the coordinator after the third final review of #668 on d78067c: option 1, narrow the PR. Keep the bounded, provider-scoped settle wait, lease waits with the atomic claim, supersede-on-timeout, fail()/destroy() through retire(), start timing and the RF-147 banner, iOS probe gate and strict desktop test. Remove all late-settle detection and the once-per-page FairPlay clear (restore the per-call clear the passing iPhone runs used). Change the stuck-play hard cap to a clear Retry error that keeps the lease until MusicKit settles. Late-settle work and the once-per-load clear move to RF-159.

Commit 62042da narrows #668 as decided: no late-settle detection (a late, superseded setQueue settle is not detected; generation guards still stop its result counting as a cue), per-call FairPlay clear restored, and a stuck cancelled play keeps its lease so Retry fails with "Apple Music is still finishing the previous song. Tap Retry." instead of starting a second play. The two hard-cap tests fail on d78067c and pass on 62042da. Mock MusicKit only.

Owner decision in session 2026-10-30, relayed by the coordinator after the fourth final review of #668 on 85442ac: option 1, measure first. #668 shrinks to the RF-128 timing instrumentation and the RF-147 cleanups that need no locks; everything else in apps/ reverts to main. The lock work (leases, settle wait, hard caps, attempt token) is preserved on wip/rf-108-apple-locks at 85442ac. After deploy the owner times Start and quick taps on the iPhone, and RF-108's locks are redesigned in a new PR around those numbers.
Branch preserving the RF-108 lock work at 85442ac (the #668 head before the shrink). Not reviewed for merge; its four review rounds are in the #668 comments.

Owner iPhone Safari timing run on production main 97f4454 with ?playback-timing=1, relayed by the conductor 2026-10-31: MusicKit ready/authorized 1-34 ms; setQueue 27-247 ms (30-60 ms warm); a cancelled adapter's setQueue kept running 129 ms and 1,125 ms; play-start to first playing state 465-1,186 ms; play() resolved 1.7-2.6 s after the call (1.1-1.4 s after audio was playing); later tracks called setQueue twice per start. Every timeline-track tap started two adapters ~60 ms apart, and the second failed with "still finishing a previous queue request" until Retry (four of four jumps); Start itself worked. Next and auto-advance were not measured. Owner approved the redesign plan in chat ("Yes, approved"): wait for a previous queue (bounded 2 s) instead of failing, remove the double start at its source, count first playing state as started with a 3 s play cap, keep the late-settle ruling (Retry, never auto-play).

Double start fixed at its source: LiveTimeline pointer down fired a leading-edge seek and pointer up flushed the same position; the trailing throttle now skips a flush equal to the value its own call just fired, and the timeline commits the gesture's previewed position. Apple adapter as merged (0a77110): a pending previous play() is superseded, not waited on; a new start waits for a previous (including cancelled) setQueue through runtime.enterTrack and whenIdle(), bounded 2 s from the cancel, then fails with the existing Retry wording and stops blocking so Retry proceeds; first playing state counts as started, and play() is capped at 5 s with a Retry error; held playback error carries an attempt token. Runtime: enterTrack re-checks the epoch before prepare. The double setQueue on later tracks is the mid-track re-cue (prepare cues the window start, the pre-play seek re-cues in play()), not the FairPlay clear; behavior left unchanged. Corrected 2026-10-31 per the #669 final review item 9 (the first version of this summary described 57a06b3: a 3 s cap and waiting for a previous play). Mock MusicKit only.

16 tests fail on main 97f4454 and pass on the PR: queue and play waits, bounded Retry error then Retry queues/plays, first playing state as started, Next waits for the previous still-pending play, 3 s play cap, attempt-token drops after destroy+prepare and after stop, timing lines, and three runtime tests with real adapters on one shared instance (taps to tracks 2 and 3 end playing track 3 with no lock error; pause then resume during a start ends playing; a never-settling cancelled setQueue fails clearly after the bound and Retry recovers). runtime.test.ts supersession tests pass unchanged.

"starts exactly one provider adapter for one timeline tap (RF-108)": pointer down, 60 ms, pointer up starts one adapter; three on main. trailing-throttle.test.ts covers the tap, drag-release and discrete-flush cases.

Final review of #669 on 57a06b3 found five significant bugs; fixed in f1fdcfd on the same PR. (1) A timeline hold or a drag that paused before release jumped the clock back behind the audio: release now sends nothing when the throttle already sent that position and settles the clock where it is, else a normal seek. (2) One bounded wait: the adapter no longer waits; runtime.enterTrack waits on whenIdle() (setQueue only, settle or 2 s from the cancel) through a page-wide registry, so Retry waits too. (3) No yield before MusicKit play() on gesture paths: a pending previous play() is superseded, not awaited, and its late settle re-asserts nothing once its queue was replaced. (4) Pause/stop during a pending play() apply at once and are re-applied when it settles; a live seek runs after it settles. (5) Destroy mid-prepare returns quietly. Mock MusicKit only.

Owner ruling 2026-10-31, relayed by the coordinator: raise the Apple play() start cap from 3 s to 5 s ("Yes"). Reason: the #669 review found a slow but successful start (~3.5 s on cellular) would be killed; the owner's Wi-Fi worst case was 1.2 s. Implemented in f1fdcfd ("did not start ... within 5 s. Retry playback.").

Hold 2 s then release, and drag then rest 2 s then release: the clock matches the provider at release and after (both fail on 57a06b3); plain tap starts one adapter; a release inside the throttle window commits once. apple-music-adapter.test.ts adds: Next right after a start reaches MusicKit play() in the same tick, pause/stop re-applied and live seek deferred while play() is pending, a cancelled setQueue settling at 1.5 s lets the next start proceed, a hung one fails once at a single bound, a 3.5 s start succeeds under the 5 s cap, destroy mid-prepare is quiet.

Final review of #669 on d0e2b52: nothing blocking; merged as 0a77110 and deployed 2026-10-31 (HISTORY). Items 2-8 are logged in RF-161; item 1 (up to about 2 s wait between a tap and play()) is part of the owner's device check; item 9 was this record's stale summary, corrected in #671.
